description_full: Fanuc Corporation engages in the development, manufacture, sale, and maintenance services of products used in automated production systems in Japan, the United States, Europe, China, the rest of Asia, and internationally. It offers CNC series, robots, and robomachine products, such as, compact machining centers, electric injection molding machines, wire electrical discharge machines; and field system basic package, and AI servo monitors, as well as servo motors, lasers. The company was incorporated in 1950 and is headquartered in Yamanashi, Japan.

financial_summary: Fanuc Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $31.8B market cap on $5.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 11% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.51× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.9%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
